summary: Morocco combines restoration, conservation and agricultural measures. Restoration includes 50,000 ha of biological reforestation and regeneration annually under the unconditional plan, 20,000 ha annually under the conditional plan, an additional 20,000 ha of forest restoration, and restoration of 30% of degraded ecosystems by 2030; the annual 50,000-ha action equals about 2.4% of current forest cover. Agriculture and mixed measures include 1.5 million ha of direct seeding (about 16.4% of current agricultural land), 1 million ha equipped with efficient irrigation by 2030, 621,000 ha of olive planting, 340,500 ha of fruit trees and 46,500 ha of citrus. Watershed management covers 1.5 million ha in 2015–2030. Conservation combines sustainable management of 30% of terrestrial and aquatic areas, marine protection across 10% of the exclusive economic zone, sustainable plans for 90% of fish stocks, and a 50% groundwater-overexploitation reduction by 2030, alongside 17 aquifer contracts and 28 large dams by 2035.
